appraisal_events.evidence: avec l'intransigeante conviction d'une wagnérienne... repoussant ainsi tout d'un coup par son interprétation l'idée qu'elle venait d'émettre... il ne faut jamais discuter le choix des amants. Mais après avoir posé ce principe, elle y manqua immédiatement en critiquant le choix de Saint-Loup
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly flags the duchesse's affected pronouncement on the mystery of love as hollow: she contradicts her own claim within the same breath, then immediately breaks the very principle of tolerance she has just proclaimed by criticizing Saint-Loup's choice again.

appraisal_events.evidence: Bloch... se mit à en dire un mal si épouvantable que tout le monde en fut révolté. Il commençait à avoir des haines... pour les assouvir il ne reculerait devant rien... déposer d'une façon mensongère... contre de telles gens toutes les armes sont permises, surtout à un Saint, comme lui, Bloch
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Bloch's vicious gossip about Saint-Loup and his willingness to give false testimony to ruin an acquaintance out of class hatred, framed with self-righteous hypocrisy, provoking open revulsion in the company.

status_effects.explanation: Her performance of philosophical broadmindedness collapses into the very small-mindedness she claims to disdain, exposed by the narrator's explicit note of her inconsistency.
His choice of lover is again singled out as baffling and unappealing, this time by the duchesse's renewed direct criticism.
The narrator lays bare a deep moral corruption in Bloch: petty class hatred, willingness to commit perjury, and self-righteous hypocrisy in calling himself a saint.
His gossip visibly revolts the whole company, a witnessed collective reaction against him within the scene.
